songs.name: He Was A Friend Of Mine

ai_show_review.summary: Scorching Lovelight sandwiches bookended by fiery Eleven & Dark Star
ai_show_review.blurb: The set erupts with a blazing Turn On Your Lovelight that rolls into tight blues‑rock before exploding into an intense Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven suite. Jerry’s guitar is possessed and mind‑melting the whole night, while the rhythm section drives a second Lovelight climax highlighted by a unique drum solo. Standout moments include The Eleven, two Lovelight explosions and a soaring Friend Of Mine.
ai_show_review.review: Monterey’s June 14, 1969 show captures the Dead at a manic peak of their early‑’69 run. Opening with an incendiary Turn On Your Lovelight that segues straight into Me And My Uncle and Doin’ That Rag, the band rides a wave of R&B grit before Pigpen’s heartfelt He Was A Friend Of Mine. Dark Star erupts into a psychedelic vortex that seamlessly morphs into Saint Stephen and then launches the legendary The Eleven – a thunder‑driven, time‑bending climax where Jerry’s lead guitar is described as “possessed” and “mind‑melting.” After a brief drum solo, the group dives back into a second Lovelight sandwich, delivering what reviewers call a “psychedelic melt‑down,” before closing the set with another turn of Lovelight. Throughout, Phil’s bass locks in tight, Mickey and Bill keep the pulse relentless, and Tom Constanten’s organ adds just enough texture to let Pigpen’s keyboards shine. Despite minor mud and a short dropout at the end of Saint Stephen, the recording captures the raw energy and improvisational daring that make this show a must‑listen for any Deadhead.

best_recording.reason: Balanced soundboard mix with full set, captures the high‑energy performance and key moments despite minor muddiness

key_highlights: Fiery Turn On Your Lovelight openings and closings bookending the set
Explosive Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven suite
Unique drum solo leading into the second Lovelight
High‑octane jams on Friend Of Mine, Me And My Uncle, and The Eleven
song_highlights: He Was A Friend Of Mine

band_performance.Jerry: Blistering, creative runs on The Eleven, Dark Star and throughout; described as possessed and mind‑melting.
band_performance.Phil: Tight, rhythmic bass work with sparkling runs during The Eleven and Saint Stephen.
band_performance.Mickey: Praised for overall rhythm section drive and a standout drum solo before the second Lovelight.
band_performance.Billy: Together with Mickey forms a relentless rhythm foundation that fuels the high‑energy set.

must_listen_sequences: He Was A Friend Of Mine
